```sh
kafka group delete-offsets <groupId>
```

Delete a consumer group's committed offsets on one or more topics

## Arguments

| Argument  | Description |
| --------- | ----------- |
| `groupId` | group id    |

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

With no --partition, clears every partition of each selected topic.

## Before you run

Removes committed checkpoints. Stop consumers and save current offsets first; their next start may replay or skip records according to reset policy.

## Flags

| Flag                                | Description                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--brokers <string>`                | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092                                                     |
| `--yes`                             | confirm the deletion without an interactive prompt                                                   |
| `--topic <string> (repeatable)`     | topic to clear (repeatable; at least one required)                                                   |
| `--partition <number> (repeatable)` | partition to clear, applied to every --topic (repeatable; defaults to every partition of each topic) |

## Examples

```sh
kafka group delete-offsets my-group --topic orders --brokers localhost:9092 --yes
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "topic": "events",
      "ok": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `4`, `5`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
